Bug Title: Market switch revalidates only the settings key so every catalog cache keeps serving the previous market
Bug Description: resolveMarketForCountry in src/helpers/market.ts:11-28 sets the market cookie at :19 - calls switchMarket at :20 - then awaits mutate('/settings') at :21 and nothing else. CLAUDE.md 7.4 requires a market switch to invalidate all catalog caches (products - categories - brands - stores - home layout - search). Those SWR keys are never mutated so they keep serving the previous market payload while /settings returns the NEW market currency symbol and format through SettingsContext at src/contexts/SettingsContext.tsx:118-128. The result is the old market prices rendered with the new market currency symbol.
Preconditions: Two markets configured with different currencies and different catalog or pricing. User has browsed a category or the home page so those SWR keys are populated.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Browse the home page and a category listing in market A so SWR caches them. 2. Change the delivery location to a country that maps to market B which calls resolveMarketForCountry. 3. Without a hard reload return to the home page or the category listing.
Expected Result: All catalog caches are invalidated on market switch so products - categories - brands - stores - home layout and search refetch under the new X-Market header.
Actual Result: Only the settings key revalidates. Catalog lists still show market A products and market A price amounts now labelled with market B currency symbol.
Impact: Customer sees another market inventory and mispriced products. Any add-to-cart from that stale list carries a product that may not be sellable in the active market.
Suggested Fix: In resolveMarketForCountry invalidate every catalog SWR key after switchMarket - either by calling mutate with a key predicate that matches the catalog endpoints or by bumping a market scoped key prefix so all catalog keys change on switch.

Bug Title: withAuth silently does nothing on checkout and payment because neither route is listed in PROTECTED_ROUTES
Bug Description: isProtectedRoute at src/guards/authGuard.ts:15-23 matches with strict equality path === route against PROTECTED_ROUTES at :5-13. That list holds /cart - /my-account - /my-account/orders - /my-account/addresses - /my-account/wallet - /my-account/transactions - /my-account/refer-and-earn. CheckoutPage is wrapped by withAuth at src/pages/cart/checkout/index.tsx:79 and its router.pathname is /cart/checkout which is not in the list. PaymentPage is wrapped at src/pages/payment/[slug].tsx:62 and its router.pathname is /payment/[slug] which is not in the list either. withAuth at src/guards/withAuth.tsx:16-25 therefore never enters its redirect branch. Neither page performs any token check in getServerSideProps - unlike the my-account pages which check getAccessTokenFromContext inline (for example src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:345-356) - so both routes are completely unguarded.
Preconditions: User is logged out. The site is running with NEXT_PUBLIC_SSR set to true.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log out or open a clean private window. 2. Navigate directly to /cart/checkout/ and then to /payment/anything.
Expected Result: The visitor is redirected away and prompted to sign in - the same behaviour the my-account routes already implement server side.
Actual Result: Both pages render for an anonymous visitor. The guard never fires because the pathname never matches the list.
Impact: Two authenticated-only routes ship with an auth control that looks present in code review but is inert. Checkout and payment shells render for anonymous users and the underlying API 401 then triggers a global logout which is a confusing dead end.
Suggested Fix: Add /cart/checkout and /payment/[slug] to PROTECTED_ROUTES and switch isProtectedRoute to a prefix match so nested and dynamic routes are covered. Better still add a server side token check to both pages in getServerSideProps so the guard does not depend on client state.

Bug Title: Bearer token and the full user record are stored in JavaScript readable cookies with no CSP in place
Bug Description: setCookie in src/lib/cookies.ts:12-51 writes cookies through document.cookie so the httpOnly flag can never be set. helpers/auth.ts stores both the bearer token and the entire user object with it at :104-105 (google) - :209-210 (apple) - :598-599 (password) and :756-757 (phone OTP). The interceptor reads the token back client side at src/routes/interceptor.ts:29. next.config.ts sets HSTS - X-Frame-Options - nosniff - Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy but sets NO Content-Security-Policy - and images.dangerouslyAllowSVG is true with remotePatterns hostname ** which widens the script injection surface. Any XSS therefore reads document.cookie and lifts a valid Sanctum bearer token plus the user name - email and mobile.
Preconditions: An XSS sink anywhere in the storefront. Note the storefront renders API supplied HTML in places which is reviewed separately in later sessions.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Trigger any script execution in the page origin. 2. Read document.cookie. 3. Replay the access_token value as an Authorization Bearer header against the panel API.
Expected Result: The session token is not reachable from page JavaScript - an httpOnly cookie still lets getAccessTokenFromContext read it server side from context.req.headers.cookie so SSR is unaffected.
Actual Result: The token and the user PII are readable by any script running on the page and there is no CSP to limit which scripts run.
Impact: Account takeover from a single XSS. The user record in the cookie also leaks name - email and mobile and is sent on every request to the domain.
Suggested Fix: Move the token to an httpOnly and secure cookie set by the backend or by a Next route handler - SSR keeps working because it reads the request header. Stop storing the whole user object in a cookie and hydrate it from the profile endpoint. Add a Content-Security-Policy header in next.config.ts.

Bug Title: handleLogout calls process.exit in its catch block which throws in the browser and would kill the server in any Node context
Bug Description: handleLogout at src/helpers/auth.ts:652-699 ends its catch with process.exit(1) at :697. In the browser process.exit is not a function so the catch itself throws a TypeError - the logout never finishes and the state left behind is inconsistent because store.dispatch(logout()) at :674 and the deleteCookie calls at :675-676 sit BEFORE the failure point only when the throw happens earlier. The catch is reachable in normal use because Router.push at :668 rejects when a route change is interrupted - for example when the user clicks another link while logout is navigating away from a my-account page. If this helper is ever evaluated in a Node context the same line terminates the process.
Preconditions: User is logged in and currently on a /my-account route so the Router.push branch at :668 executes.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in and open /my-account/orders/. 2. Trigger logout and immediately click another navigation link so the pending Router.push is interrupted and rejects. 3. Observe the catch executes process.exit.
Expected Result: Logout fails safely - the error is logged and the local session is still cleared so the user is not left in a half logged out state.
Actual Result: The catch throws a TypeError on process.exit so logout aborts. The user can remain with cookies or Redux state that disagree about whether they are signed in.
Impact: A half completed logout leaves a valid token in the cookie while the UI may show a signed out state - and the same line would terminate a Node process outright.
Suggested Fix: Remove the process.exit(1) call. Log the error and fall through to the same cleanup the success path performs so the local session is always cleared even when the logout API call or the navigation fails.

Bug Title: verifyUser converts every failure into a success false fallback so the email and phone availability check fails open and its caller error branch is unreachable
Bug Description: verifyUser at src/services/auth.ts:17-28 catches every error and returns fallbackApiRes which is success false with data undefined (src/config/constants.ts:33-37). checkEmailExists at src/helpers/auth.ts:396-436 and checkPhoneExists at :439-478 then test response.success || response.data?.exists at :412 and :455. Because the service already swallowed the rejection the try block never throws - so the catch at :420-432 that discriminates on the message User not found can never run and is dead code. A genuine network failure or a 500 from the panel is therefore indistinguishable from the user does not exist and the field is silently marked available.
Preconditions: Registration form open. The panel returns an error status when the identifier is not found which is what the dead catch at :426 was written for.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the register form. 2. Take the panel API offline or force a 500 on /verify-user. 3. Enter an email address that is already registered and leave the field.
Expected Result: The availability check fails closed or surfaces a check error to the user - the dead catch branch was written to do exactly this.
Actual Result: No error is shown. The email reads as available and registration is attempted with an address that is already taken so the failure only surfaces later from the register call.
Impact: Users are pushed into a registration attempt that cannot succeed and receive a late and confusing error. The intended error handling in the caller is unreachable code.
Suggested Fix: Let verifyUser surface the failure - either rethrow or return a discriminated result that separates request failed from user not found - then have checkEmailExists and checkPhoneExists branch on data.exists alone and show the check error state on a real failure.

Bug Title: SettingsProvider rebuilds its context value on every render so every consumer in the app re-renders
Bug Description: SettingsProvider at src/contexts/SettingsContext.tsx:69-166 builds the provider value as an inline object literal at :143-160 with no useMemo. formatPrice at :127-128 and defaultLocation at :130-139 are new references on every render as well. The provider wraps the application so every component calling useSettings at :67 re-renders whenever the provider renders - even when settings itself is unchanged. Every derived value from :76-125 is also recomputed on each render including the six getSpecificSettings scans over the settings array.
Preconditions: Any page - the provider is mounted app wide.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Render any page that has several useSettings consumers such as a product listing with prices. 2. Trigger a parent re-render. 3. Observe every consumer re-renders although settings did not change.
Expected Result: The context value is memoised on the settings identity so consumers only re-render when settings actually changes.
Actual Result: A new value object is created on every render so all consumers re-render and all derived settings are recomputed.
Impact: App wide unnecessary re-render cost on the busiest screens - product grids read currency formatting from this context for every price shown.
Suggested Fix: Wrap the derived values and the provider value in useMemo keyed on settings and wrap formatPrice in useCallback so the identity is stable across renders.

Bug Title: The response interceptor writes to the maintenance store on every successful response and notifies all subscribers each time
Bug Description: The response interceptor at src/routes/interceptor.ts:66-73 calls maintenanceStore.setMaintenance(false - null) for every 2xx response. setMaintenance at src/stores/maintenanceStore.ts:17-25 assigns a brand new state object and then calls every registered listener unconditionally - there is no check for whether the state actually changed. Subscribers therefore receive a change notification and a new state identity after every single API call even though maintenance mode was already inactive.
Preconditions: Any subscriber mounted - the layouts subscribe to render the maintenance banner.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a page that issues several API calls such as the home page. 2. Observe setMaintenance runs once per response and notifies every listener with a fresh object identity.
Expected Result: The store only notifies subscribers when the maintenance state actually changes.
Actual Result: Every successful response allocates a new state object and wakes every subscriber which re-renders the subscribing layout.
Impact: Wasted renders on every API call across the whole app - the cost scales with the number of requests a screen makes.
Suggested Fix: Return early in setMaintenance when isActive and message already equal the incoming values so listeners fire only on a real transition.

Bug Title: getCookie truncates any cookie value that contains an equals sign
Bug Description: getCookie at src/lib/cookies.ts:54-70 splits each cookie on = with const [key - value] = cookie.trim().split('=') at :61 and keeps only the first two segments. Any value containing an = is cut at the first one. Values written by setCookie survive because setCookie encodes with encodeURIComponent at :29-31 which turns = into %3D - but a cookie set by the backend is not necessarily encoded. src/services/market.ts:28-32 documents that the backend sets the market cookie itself on /markets/switch and the interceptor reads that cookie client side at src/routes/interceptor.ts:48 to build the X-Market header. Base64 or JWT style values with = padding are the common case that breaks.
Preconditions: A cookie written by the backend rather than by setCookie whose value contains an = character.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Have the backend set a cookie whose value contains = such as base64 padding. 2. Read it client side through getCookie. 3. Compare the returned value with document.cookie.
Expected Result: The full cookie value is returned regardless of any = characters inside it.
Actual Result: The value is truncated at the first = and the caller receives a corrupted value or null once JSON.parse fails.
Impact: A truncated market cookie sends a wrong or empty X-Market header so the client silently falls back to the default market - the failure mode section 7.4 of CLAUDE.md warns about.
Suggested Fix: Split on the first = only - for example by using indexOf and slice - and decode the key as well as the value.

Bug Title: serverSideAuthGuard is dead code while ten account pages each reimplement the same check inline
Bug Description: serverSideAuthGuard at src/guards/authGuard.ts:39-64 is exported and documented in CLAUDE.md 7.5 as the primary protection mechanism but no page calls it - a search across src/pages returns only the CLAUDE.md documentation reference. Instead ten my-account pages import loginRedirect directly and repeat the same getAccessTokenFromContext check plus redirect block inline - src/pages/my-account/index.tsx:12 - orders/index.tsx:23 - orders/[slug]/index.tsx:19 - addresses/index.tsx:22 - wallet/index.tsx:26 - transactions/index.tsx:20 - profile/index.tsx:58 - notifications/index.tsx:26 - wishlists/index.tsx:10 and refer-and-earn/index.tsx:14. The duplicated block is visible at orders/index.tsx:345-356.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Search src/pages for serverSideAuthGuard and observe there are no callers. 2. Compare the inline guard in any two my-account pages and observe the block is copy pasted.
Expected Result: One shared guard is called by every protected page as CLAUDE.md 7.5 prescribes.
Actual Result: The shared guard is unused and the same logic is duplicated across ten pages so a fix to the redirect behaviour has to be made ten times.
Impact: Divergence risk - a page added later can silently omit the block which is exactly what happened to checkout and payment in issue 2. Documented architecture and real code disagree.
Suggested Fix: Have each protected page call serverSideAuthGuard at the top of getServerSideProps and return its result when it is not null - then delete the inline duplicates.

Bug Title: The wildcard branch in isProtectedRoute is unreachable because no route entry uses the suffix it tests for
Bug Description: isProtectedRoute at src/guards/authGuard.ts:15-23 tests route.endsWith('/*') at :17 and strips the suffix at :18 to do a startsWith prefix match at :19. No entry in PROTECTED_ROUTES at :5-13 ends with /* so that branch never executes and every comparison falls through to the strict equality at :21. The prefix matching capability the function appears to offer does not exist in practice which is the mechanism behind issue 2.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Read PROTECTED_ROUTES at src/guards/authGuard.ts:5-13. 2. Confirm no entry ends with /*. 3. Confirm the branch at :17-19 is therefore never taken.
Expected Result: Either the route list uses the wildcard form the function supports or the dead branch is removed.
Actual Result: The branch is dead code and gives a false impression that nested routes are covered.
Impact: A reviewer or a future contributor reads the function as supporting prefix matching and adds a nested protected route expecting it to be covered when it is not.
Suggested Fix: Either add the wildcard entries the function was written for such as /my-account/* and /cart/* or drop the branch and make the prefix matching explicit.

Bug Title: The any type is used in the interceptor 503 handler and across the market service against the strict TypeScript rule
Bug Description: CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids any and requires unknown API shapes to get a type in src/types first. The 503 branch of the response interceptor casts the payload twice at src/routes/interceptor.ts:99 and :102 with (responseData as any) to read the maintenance flag and the message. src/services/market.ts declares both endpoints as ApiResponse<any> at :16 and :35 so geoDetectForCountry and switchMarket return untyped data - and the caller in src/helpers/market.ts:17 then reaches into res?.data?.suggested_market with no type safety at all.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Read src/routes/interceptor.ts:96-103. 2. Read src/services/market.ts:14-43 and the consumer at src/helpers/market.ts:17.
Expected Result: Both the maintenance payload and the market endpoints have declared types in src/types and no any appears.
Actual Result: Four any usages remain and the market switch payload is entirely untyped on a path that decides which market the whole catalog is scoped to.
Impact: A response shape change in the market or maintenance payload passes the type checker silently and only fails at runtime - and this is the exact path that controls market scoping.
Suggested Fix: Add a MaintenanceResponse type and a GeoDetect and MarketSwitch response type in src/types and use them in place of the any casts.

Bug Title: Anonymous server side requests log a token message on every render
Bug Description: getAccessTokenFromContext at src/helpers/auth.ts:701-729 writes console.log('No valid token found in SSR context') at :723 on every server side render where no token cookie is present. That is every anonymous visit to any page whose getServerSideProps calls it. The message is noise rather than a leak - no token value is printed - but it runs on the hot SSR path and buries real errors in production logs.
Preconditions: Site running with NEXT_PUBLIC_SSR set to true and an anonymous visitor.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run the app in SSR mode. 2. Request any page whose getServerSideProps calls getAccessTokenFromContext while logged out. 3. Read the server log.
Expected Result: No log line for the ordinary anonymous case - an absent token is expected rather than exceptional.
Actual Result: One console.log per anonymous server side render.
Impact: Production log noise proportional to anonymous traffic which makes real errors harder to find. Note that compiler.removeConsole in next.config.ts strips console.log in production builds so the impact is limited to non production and to any build where that option is changed.
Suggested Fix: Drop the log line or lower it to a debug level guarded by an explicit flag.

Bug Title: Password and other credentials are sent in the URL query string instead of the request body
Bug Description: login at src/services/auth.ts:69-83 calls api.post with the /login path - a null body - and a params object at :77 so email - password and mobile are serialised into the query string rather than the body. The same pattern repeats at :32 for registerUser where password and password_confirmation are sent to /register - at :22 for verifyUser (/verify-user) and at :201 for forgotPassword (/forget-password). axios places the params object in the URL and sends a null body so the full credential set appears in the request line. Every hop that records request lines keeps them - web server access logs - reverse proxies - CDNs and APM traces. Contrast phoneLogin at :119-138 which correctly sends a body and moves only the bearer token into a header so the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
Preconditions: Any login or registration attempt. Standard web server or proxy access logging which records the request line including the query string.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the login sheet and submit any email and password. 2. Inspect the outgoing request in the devtools network tab and read the request URL. 3. Confirm the password appears as a query parameter while the request body is null.
Expected Result: Credentials travel in the POST body only and never appear in the URL.
Actual Result: email - password - mobile and password_confirmation are all query parameters on the request URL.
Impact: Plaintext passwords are written into every access log and proxy log along the request path and are readable by anyone with log access. Because users reuse passwords the exposure reaches beyond this application. Log shipping and retention widen it further.
Suggested Fix: Send these payloads as the request body rather than as params for /login - /register - /verify-user and /forget-password. Confirm the panel accepts body parameters on those routes first and coordinate the change because the API is shared with other production clients.

Bug Title: The bearer token and the full user record are persisted to localStorage by redux-persist
Bug Description: The redux-persist configuration at src/lib/redux/store.ts:12-16 lists auth in the whitelist so the entire auth slice is serialised to localStorage under the persist key root. authSlice at src/lib/redux/slices/authSlice.ts:5-15 holds access_token and the complete user object so both are written on every login through the login reducer at :26-30. This is a SECOND copy of the session and is distinct from issue 3 which covers the JavaScript readable cookie - the fix differs because this one is redux-persist configuration rather than cookie flags. localStorage also has no expiry so this copy outlives the cookie.
Preconditions: Any logged in session.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log in. 2. Open the devtools application tab and read the localStorage key persist:root. 3. Find access_token and the user object inside the serialised auth slice.
Expected Result: The session token is not written to localStorage - persist only non sensitive auth fields such as isLoggedIn and rehydrate the session from the cookie or the profile endpoint.
Actual Result: access_token and the full user record including name - email and mobile are stored in localStorage in clear text with no expiry.
Impact: A second XSS reachable copy of the bearer token plus user PII. Because localStorage never expires the token survives a browser restart and remains replayable on a shared machine long after the cookie has gone.
Suggested Fix: Remove auth from the redux-persist whitelist or add a persist transform that strips access_token and the user PII before serialisation - then rehydrate auth state on boot from the session cookie or from /user/profile.

Bug Title: The cart slice is persisted although both CLAUDE files explicitly forbid persisting it
Bug Description: The redux-persist whitelist at src/lib/redux/store.ts:16 contains cart. Root CLAUDE.md section 7.1 lists the allowlist as auth - offlineCart - recentlyViewed and search - and src/lib/redux/CLAUDE.md states plainly that cart must not be persisted because it is a server mirror that is always re-fetched on login. cartSlice is persisted anyway so a stale server cart is rehydrated from localStorage on every boot and rendered before any revalidation completes. Separately search is absent from the whitelist which also contradicts root CLAUDE.md 7.1 - but the inline comment at :16 shows that exclusion is deliberate so only the cart entry is treated as a defect here.
Preconditions: Logged in user with items in the server cart. The cart has since changed elsewhere - another device or an admin action or a price change.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Add items to the cart and allow the state to persist. 2. Change that cart from another device or change a product price server side. 3. Reopen the storefront and read the cart before the refetch resolves.
Expected Result: The cart is not persisted - it is fetched from the server so the first paint shows either server truth or a loading state.
Actual Result: The previous cart is rehydrated from localStorage and rendered including stale quantities and stale prices until the refetch replaces it.
Impact: Customer briefly sees outdated cart contents and pricing which is most visible on a slow connection. The documented state ownership and the shipped configuration disagree which will mislead the next person to read either CLAUDE file.
Suggested Fix: Remove cart from the whitelist so the server mirror is always fetched. If persisting it is a deliberate offline decision then update both CLAUDE files to match and document what guarantees revalidation before the cart is shown.

Bug Title: Firebase auth error messages and setup toasts are hard-coded English and bypass i18n
Bug Description: getFirebaseErrorMessage at src/lib/firebase.ts:247-271 returns twelve hard-coded English strings for the Firebase auth error codes it maps at :251 :253 :255 :257 :259 :261 :263 :265 and :267 - and falls back to the raw Firebase SDK error.message at :269. Those strings reach users through addToast in src/helpers/auth.ts at :265 for apple login - :322 for sign up and :386 for resend OTP - code which uses i18n.t for every other string it renders. src/lib/firebase.ts also raises English toasts directly at :88-90 - :129-131 - :214-217 and :221-224. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any Firebase auth failure such as an expired code or the too many requests limit.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Request a phone OTP and enter an incorrect code or trigger the too many attempts limit. 3. Read the toast that appears.
Expected Result: The message renders in the active language from the locale bundles like every other auth message in the same flow.
Actual Result: The message renders in English whatever the selected language - and the default branch can surface a raw Firebase SDK string that was never written for end users.
Impact: Hindi and Arabic users meet untranslated English at the exact moment authentication fails which is a high friction point in the funnel. The default branch can also leak raw SDK wording into the UI.
Suggested Fix: Map each Firebase error code to a translation key and resolve it with t() at the call site - add the keys to en - hi and ar - and give the default branch a generic translated fallback instead of error.message. Then run npm run scan:i18n.

Bug Title: The offline cart is cleared on login even when the server rejected some items so those items are lost
Bug Description: syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:77-160 dispatches clearOfflineCart() at :110 as soon as response.success is true - before it inspects response.data.failed_items at :113. Items the server refused (out of stock - not sellable in the active market - variant gone) are therefore deleted from the only local copy the user has. The failed list is passed to a modal at :119 through the window global showFailedItemsModal - which is registered by src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 and DELETED again at :41 when that component unmounts - so if the modal is not mounted at that moment the guard at :115-118 is false and the user is told nothing at all. Either way the items are already gone from state and cannot be retried or recovered.
Preconditions: User has items in the offline cart while logged out and at least one of them is rejected by the server on sync - for example an item that went out of stock or is not sellable in the active market.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. While logged out add two products to the cart and let the offline cart persist. 2. Make one of them unsellable server side - out of stock or removed from the active market. 3. Log in and let the sync run. 4. Read the cart and the offline cart state.
Expected Result: Rejected items stay in the offline cart (or are surfaced with a retry) so the customer keeps what they chose and can act on it.
Actual Result: The whole offline cart is cleared regardless of failures. The failed items exist only inside a transient modal payload and are unrecoverable once it closes or if it never opened.
Impact: Silent loss of items the customer deliberately added. The most likely moment for this is the login that happens at the start of checkout so it directly costs conversions and the customer may not notice items are missing before paying.
Suggested Fix: Clear only the items the server accepted - keep any id present in failed_items in the offline cart - and surface the failure through normal React state rather than a window global that may not exist. Dispatch setOfflineCart with the remainder instead of clearOfflineCart.

Bug Title: clampQuantity can return a quantity below the product minimum and its second branch is unreachable
Bug Description: clampQuantity at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:55-85 first clamps into the min and max and stock window at :61-64 then snaps to the step size. The stepSize > 1 branch at :66-73 snaps to an absolute multiple of stepSize and never re-checks minQuantity - so a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2 given a desired quantity of 3 yields qty 3 at :61 - then remainder 3 % 2 = 1 at :67 - then qty = 2 at :69 - and the guard at :70 compares against stepSize rather than minQuantity so 2 is not raised back. The function returns 2 for a product whose minimum is 3. The else branch at :74-82 is dead code because it is reached only when stepSize is 1 (item.stepSize || 1 at :57 makes 0 impossible) and any value modulo 1 is 0 - so its remainder at :75 is always 0. Note the two branches also encode different models - absolute multiples in one and offsets from minQuantity in the other.
Preconditions: A product configured with a minimum quantity above 1 and a step size above 1 where the minimum is not itself a multiple of the step.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Configure a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2. 2. While logged out add it to the cart with quantity 3. 3. Read the stored offline cart quantity.
Expected Result: The quantity respects the product minimum and the step rule together - the nearest valid value at or above the minimum.
Actual Result: The quantity is snapped down to 2 which is below the configured minimum of 3.
Impact: Customer can build an offline cart that breaks the seller minimum order rule. It surfaces at login sync or at add-to-cart as a server rejection which then triggers the item loss described in issue 17.
Suggested Fix: Snap to the step relative to minQuantity and re-clamp upward afterwards so the result is never below minQuantity - and delete the unreachable else branch so a single model applies.

Bug Title: updateCartData decides the empty-cart case by string matching an English API message
Bug Description: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:15-75 tests cartRes.message == 'Your cart is empty' at :49 to choose the empty-cart branch. CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids hard-coding status strings and the panel message is free text that other clients also consume. If the wording changes or is ever localised server side the comparison silently fails and control falls into the else at :59 which dispatches setError and raises a Cart Fetch Failed toast - so a normal empty cart is reported to the customer as a system failure and the checkout state is never reset by resetCheckOutState at :51.
Preconditions: The panel returns success false with a message for the empty-cart case and that wording changes or is localised.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Empty the cart. 2. Change the panel message for the empty cart response or request it in a non English locale. 3. Reload the cart and read the UI.
Expected Result: The empty cart renders the empty state and the checkout state is reset - keyed off a stable field such as a status code or an item count rather than prose.
Actual Result: The empty cart is treated as a fetch failure - an error toast is shown and resetCheckOutState never runs so stale promo and wallet selections survive.
Impact: A routine empty cart is presented as a broken page. Because resetCheckOutState is skipped a stale promo code or wallet flag can carry into the next order.
Suggested Fix: Branch on a stable machine readable field - a status code or the item count on the payload - instead of the message text. If the panel has no such field request one and flag the contract gap rather than changing the shape unilaterally.

Bug Title: Cart status toasts are hard-coded English and one contains a typo
Bug Description: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts raises four user-facing strings with no translation - title Cart is Empty and description Add Product to processed ! at :54-55 and title Cart Fetch Failed and description Could not update cart after adding item at :63-64. The same file uses i18n.t elsewhere for the sync toasts at :126-129 so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar. The description at :55 also reads Add Product to processed ! which is not grammatical English and appears to be intended as proceed.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any empty cart or failed cart refresh.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Empty the cart or force the cart refresh to fail. 3. Read the toast.
Expected Result: The toast renders in the active language from the locale bundles.
Actual Result: The toast renders in English in every language and shows the malformed sentence Add Product to processed !.
Impact: Hindi and Arabic customers meet untranslated and grammatically broken English inside the cart which is a high intent part of the funnel.
Suggested Fix: Move all four strings into the locale bundles under a cart namespace - fix the wording to proceed - add the keys to en hi and ar and run npm run scan:i18n.

Bug Title: Merging two offline cart lines adds their quantities without applying the clamp so stock and maximum limits are bypassed
Bug Description: updateOfflineCartItem at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:179-213 handles the case where editing addons changes an item id. When the new id already exists it merges with a bare addition at :198 - state.items[nextIndex].quantity += action.payload.newItem.quantity - and then splices the old line at :199. clampQuantity is never applied to that sum even though every other write path in the slice applies it - addOfflineCartItem at :126-129 and updateOfflineCartItemQuantity at :164-167 both clamp. The merged line can therefore exceed maxQuantity and exceed stock and can also break the step rule.
Preconditions: Two offline cart lines for the same variant that differ only by addons where their combined quantity exceeds the stock or the maximum quantity.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. While logged out add a product with addon set A and again with addon set B so two lines exist. 2. Edit one line so its addons match the other and the ids collide. 3. Read the merged quantity against the product stock and maximum.
Expected Result: The merged quantity is clamped to the stock - maximum and step rules exactly as the other write paths clamp.
Actual Result: The two quantities are summed unchecked so the line can exceed the stock and the maximum quantity.
Impact: An offline cart that violates stock and quantity limits reaches the login sync and is rejected there - which then destroys the items through issue 17. The subtotal shown to the customer before login is also wrong.
Suggested Fix: Apply clampQuantity to the summed quantity at :198 exactly as addOfflineCartItem does at :126-129 - ideally by routing every quantity write through one shared helper so a future path cannot skip it.

Bug Title: Cart flows drive modals through a hidden DOM button click and a window global instead of React state
Bug Description: Two cross-component signals in the cart path bypass React entirely. updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:47 calls document.getElementById('removed-items-modal-open')?.click() to open the removed-items notice - the target is a hidden button rendered by src/components/Modals/RemovedItemsModal.tsx:62 and read back at :40. syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:115-119 calls the window global showFailedItemsModal which src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 assigns on mount and deletes at :41 on unmount - and the call is cast through (window as any) which also breaches the no any rule in CLAUDE.md section 5. Both signals fail silently when the target component is not mounted and neither is type checked.
Preconditions: The modal component is not mounted on the current route when the signal fires.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Trigger a cart refresh that returns removed_count above zero or a login sync that returns failed_items on a route where the matching modal is not mounted. 2. Observe that nothing opens and no error is raised.
Expected Result: Cross-component signals travel through React state or a store so they are type checked and cannot be lost.
Actual Result: The click target or the window function is absent so the notification is dropped without any diagnostic.
Impact: The customer is never told that items were removed from the cart or rejected during sync. It also makes the flow untestable and invisible to the type checker.
Suggested Fix: Replace both with state - a store flag or a context that the modals subscribe to - so the signal is typed and survives regardless of mount order. This also removes the two (window as any) casts.
